tagline: A leading international owner and operator of container vessels
hero_kpi_rationale: The number of transportable containers (TEU) is the primary revenue driver in maritime shipping. For Costamare, it is the best indicator of its competitive position and ability to capture global shipping demand.

kpis.name: Fleet size (in thousands of containers)
kpis.explanation: Total number of 20-foot containers (TEU) that the fleet can transport.
kpis.description: Costamare's fleet comprises 73 vessels with total capacity of approximately 731,000 TEU as of December 31, 2025.
kpis.signal: Organic fleet growth through targeted acquisitions

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Money earned from leasing container ships.
kpis.description: Revenue increased in 2025, supported by a tight shipping market.
kpis.signal: Revenue growth driven by high freight rates and strong utilization

kpis.name: Operating margin
kpis.description: Operating margin improved in 2025, driven by favorable charter rates.
kpis.signal: Improved profitability from long-term contracts and cost management

kpis.name: Capital expenditures
kpis.explanation: Money spent to purchase or modernize vessels.
kpis.description: Capex increased in 2025 with advance payments for six vessels under construction and acquisition of container ship Maersk Puelo, totaling $179M in cash used for investing activities.
kpis.signal: Increased capex for newbuild acquisitions and modernizations

kpis.name: Total headcount
kpis.explanation: Number of people employed by the company.
kpis.description: Costamare employs approximately 55 people at headquarters; vessel management is outsourced.
kpis.signal: Very lean headcount typical of maritime management companies

kpis.name: Long-term contracts share
kpis.explanation: Proportion of vessels leased under contracts longer than one year.
kpis.description: 85% of the fleet is committed under long-term charters, reducing revenue volatility.
kpis.signal: Revenue stability assured by long-term contracts

risks.title: Increased competition on charter rates
risks.score_rationale: The risk is central in Item 1A, mentioned at the outset of sector risks with strong language ("material adverse impact"). Trend is upward with an orderbook at 33.9% of existing fleet, the highest level since 2011. Competition category is strategic for shipping operations.

risks.title: Dependence on charterers for payments
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in operational risks with concerning language ("adversely affect"). Risk is stable but critical, linked to customer financial health. Credit category is central to Costamare's business model.

risks.title: Increasing customs and tariff regulations
risks.score_rationale: Central position in the document, with recent developments (USTR port fees 2025, maritime plan 2026). Very strong language ("material adverse impact") and clearly worsening trend. Regulation category is critical here.

risks.title: Reduction in Chinese exports
risks.score_rationale: Though macroeconomic, this risk is specifically tied to global container trade structure. Mentioned with emphasis, downward trend in Chinese exports, and direct impact on demand. Macro category justified by its sector weight.

risks.title: Pirate attacks and regional conflicts
risks.score_rationale: Risk highlighted with concrete examples (Houthi attacks in Red Sea). Alarming language ("marine disaster", "terrorism"). Trend worsening in 2025-2026. Geopolitical category highly relevant.

risks.title: Dependence on third-party management
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in operational risks, with concerning language about managers' ability to attract qualified crews. Trend stable, but structural risk. Industrial category justified by operational model.

risks.title: Conflicts of interest with management
risks.score_rationale: Risk specifically mentioned for CEO and ties with managers. Measured but recurring language. Trend stable. Key-person category justified by internal control exposure.

risks.title: New construction risks
risks.score_rationale: Key risk in growth section, with strong language ("adversely affect"). Trend uncertain with future deliveries. Industrial category relevant for fleet renewal projects.

ai_positioning.summary: Costamare does not mention any AI initiatives in its financial or operational documents. The company follows a traditional fleet management strategy with no signals of disruptive technology adoption.
evidence: Exclusive focus on charter contracts and vessel acquisition
